name: .454 High Pressure
description:
The .454 High Pressure is the spiritual descendant of the old .454 Casull, a round that was already excessive by 20th-century standards and has only gotten more so with modern propellant chemistry. The 'High Pressure' designation is not marketing language — this round operates at chamber pressures that will destroy most revolvers not specifically rated for it, and the ammunition is stamped with a GLMZ Munitions Safety Board warning in three languages and two pictograms. Modern loads use a synthetic-wrapped brass case that handles the pressure spike better than old brass, and the projectile is typically a bonded hollow-point or solid copper design depending on whether you want expansion or penetration through vehicle doors.

In GLMZ 2200, .454 High Pressure is a niche round with a specific market: people dealing with threats that require it. That means enforcement contractors working industrial zones where heavy exoskeleton labor units occasionally malfunction catastrophically, Excluded hunters in the outer collapse zones who encounter feral augmented animals, and the kind of Tier 3 private security specialist who gets paid to think about what happens if the threat is wearing hard plate. It's not a street round — it's too loud, too expensive, and the revolvers that chamber it weigh as much as a small carbine. But when it works, it works with authority that nothing in the same price tier matches.
compatibility_note: Compatible only with heavy-frame revolvers specifically rated for .454 pressure specifications, including the Halverson H-454 'Sledge' and Drevko D-Magnum line. Also chambers in some single-shot hunting pistols. Will also fire .45 Colt in compatible revolvers. Not suitable for any semi-automatic platform.
reliability_note: Brass-polymer hybrid case, high-pressure gunpowder load. The round itself is reliable; the weapons that chamber it require regular inspection of cylinder and forcing cone for pressure-related wear. Functions in all weather conditions. No electronic dependency. Extremely loud — suppression is impractical.
